Job Type:
Open & Promotional (Dual)

Definition

Plans, coordinates, budgets, and manages assigned college construction and renovation projects from the initial planning phase through final completion to ensure that projects and successfully delivered within budget, schedule, and in compliance with regulatory guidelines and District specifications.

Typical Duties

Assists college administrators with the development of building, construction, and renovation plans by meeting and consulting with architects, engineers, and appropriate college and District staff.

Provides details, technical project descriptions, and specifications for contract architects and/or architectural and engineering staff.

Gathers data, develops project budgets, and implements appropriate budgetary control procedures for all phases including design, construction, and group II equipment.

Prepares applications for projects and submits project information for review or approval to the Board of Trustees, California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office, and others.

Coordinates projects with ongoing or proposed major maintenance programs, equipment needs, land acquisition, project design, contract solicitation, project inspection, and the Division of the State Architect.

Maintains liaison with college administration throughout planning and construction phases to provide information on project operations and progress and to receive input on the plans, schedules, interests, and concerns of the college regarding the project.

Identifies and updates project risks periodically, and creates and updates risk mitigation plans.

Meets with college maintenance and operations staff to confer on matters that may impact their ability to effectively maintain and operate the facility under construction.

Responds to concerns, requests, and questions from college administration regarding the project.

Monitors the entry of data related to approved projects and facilities inventory into the District's computerized reporting system.

Provides ongoing management of multiple assigned construction/renovation projects representing the interests of college and District administrations including directions to the architect, engineer, and construction inspector, project design, implementation of budget controls, project bid ability, construct ability, bid specifications, change orders, administration of various contracts, management of the inspection, and other project management requirements during the preliminary planning, documentation bidding, and construction phases of various projects.

Assists in the review and approval of contractors' proposed construction schedules.

Assists in the review and evaluation of construction project progress and approval of requests for payment.

Monitors construction document status, submittals, and as-build drawing preparation.

Reviews requests for clarification and assists in interpretation of construction documents.

Assists in processing and negotiating cost, scheduling change orders, and resolving complex construction related disputes.

Coordinates project close-out and move-in activities.

Interfaces and assists fiscal services in reconciliation of the Capital Outlay Fund to the general ledger and the filing of claims for reimbursement.

Assists in the coordination of construction planning events with purchasing and contracts for scheduling and acquisition of equipment.

Advises commissioned architects, engineers, consultants, and contractors about District design and construction policies, requirements, and standards.

Performs related duties as assigned.

Distinguishing Characteristics

A Facilities Project Manager
plans, coordinates, budgets, and manages multiple assigned college building construction and renovation, modernization, and repair projects throughout project development, design, and construction to ensure that projects are successfully delivered within budget, schedule, and in compliance with regulatory guidelines and District specifications. The projects range in complexity and typical values of $0.2 million to $5 million.

A Construction Inspector
serves as the resident inspector for the District at construction sites; performs continuous inspection of all phases of assigned construction including materials, methods, and workmanship; and checks for compliance with plans, specifications, and regulations. An incumbent in this classification must possess a Class 1 inspector certification issued by the Division of the State Architect.

A Director of Facilities Planning and Development
assists the Chief Facilities Executive by assuming administrative and technical responsibility and authority for delegated program areas and projects; supervising daily division activities and personnel; and assuming responsibility for the Chief Facilities Executive in their absence.

Supervision

General supervision is received from the Director of Facilities Planning and Development. Functional supervision is exercised over commissioned architects, engineers, consultants, and contractors employed by the District on an assigned project.

Class Qualifications

Knowledge of:

Principles of facilities planning as related to methods and techniques of instruction, traffic flow, economy of maintenance, provision for growth, relationship of instructional and service provision of temporary facilities, and adaptability to multi-functional usage

General characteristics and relative costs of various methods of construction, architectural features, and building and room design for all types of school uses

Principles of project management including business case development, project selection criteria, stakeholder identification techniques, and risk identification and assessment

Principles of architectural and engineering design

Principles of budgetary planning and management

Principles of construction scheduling

Characteristics and use of various methods of graphic presentation and construction documentation cartography

Principles of construction technology and construction management

Construction delivery methods such as Design-Build, Design-Bid-Build, etc.

Applicable state and local building codes/regulations and review procedures

Recordkeeping procedures

Project review/approval processes

Close out requirements and processes

Capabilities of computer applications, systems, and hardware used in facilities planning and development

Ability To

Effectively structure, integrate, and control all aspects of a project including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling, and closing

Manage a team of professionals in construction, engineering, and architectural disciplines

Maintain focus and quality under distracting working conditions and high workloads

Manage project budget and expenses in a manner consistent with achieving project quality, schedules, and levels of service

Understand audit and oversight functions and the impact of quality assurance reviews and inspection

Represent the interests of college and District administrations relative to assigned projects

Analyze and interpret complex information and make appropriate recommendations

Read and interpret architectural plans and specifications

Interpret technical materials such as building and attendance codes, standards, and regulations

Assure compliance with project requirements and standards

Anticipate conditions, plan ahead, establish priorities, and meet schedules

Act independently and promptly to situations and events

Travel to on-site and off-site meetings

Travel to various locations to monitor project progress

Prepare clear, concise, and effective oral and written communications, reports, and presentations

Maintain accurate and complete records

Effectively collaborate with external regulatory, governmental, and business or customer groups

Communicate effectively with architects, consultants, contractors, and District administrators

Effectively utilize computer equipment, software, and hardware in the performance of duties

Learn specialized software applications

Education and Experience:

A bachelor's degree from a recognized college or university, preferably with a major in architecture, construction management, engineering, urban planning, or a related field AND four years of full-time, paid, professional-level experience in planning facilities or managing the construction of educational, governmental, or commercial building projects. Experience with the project life cycle and planning and construction of educational facilities is highly desirable.

OR

Possession of a current Project Management Professional (PMP) certification from the Project Management Institute or equivalent such as successful completion of a recognized college-level project management curriculum OR a Certified Construction Manager (CCM) certification from the Construction Management Association of America AND five years of full-time, paid, professional-level experience in planning facilities or managing the construction of educational, governmental, or commercial building projects. Experience with the project life cycle and planning and construction of educational facilities is highly desirable.

Special

A valid Class "C" California driver's license is required.

Travel to locations throughout the District is required.

A $50,000 life insurance policy is provided free of charge for each employee.

19 paid holidays per year.

Summary

Organizational Location: This position is with the Department of Homeland Security, within U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Facilities and Asset Management (OFAM), Mission Support Facilities (MSF) Division. There are (2) vacancies that may be filled in one of the following locations: Indianapolis, IN Aliso Viejo, CA Euless, TX Washington, DC Additional selections may be made for other organizational divisions and/or units within the duty location(s) listed above.

Duties

This position is with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), within U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Office of Facilities and Asset Management (OFAM),Mission Support Facilities (MSF) Division. Mission Support Facilities Division provides the facilities and associated infrastructure, facilities management, and sustainment to support CBP mission support office operations. As stewards of a large national portfolio of GSA-owned and CBP-owned infrastructure, MSF carefully balances resources to ensure the right facilities are planned and delivered at the right time to meet mission requirements. The Enterprise Facilities Support (EFS)Program Management Office (PMO) is comprised of three branches - Facilities and Infrastructure Management, Housing, and Program Management. These branches are responsible for the planning, development, and execution of facility projects, handling maintenance and repairs, and coordinating/evaluating Facility Condition Assessments for all mission support facilities outside of the National Capital Region, including CBP's portfolio of residential housing. This position starts at a salary of $106,437.00 (GS-13, Step 1) to $138,370.00 (GS-13, Step 10). Salary: Salary listed reflects the rest of U.S. scale and, if applicable, will be adjusted to meet the locality pay or cost of living expenses of the duty location upon selection. GS Salary: Visit this link to view the locality pay tables by geographic area. If you do not see your geographic area listed, select the "Rest of United States" pay table. Some positions fall under a special pay rate depending on the series, grade level and location of the position. Please visit this link to view special pay rate charts. Typical work assignments include: Coordinating collaboratively with CBP organizations that EFS services to evaluate and refine their facility requirements into formal Requirements Development Requests (RDRs). Leading the optimal conversion of RDRs into viable projects that are frequently executed by other government agencies, primarily the General Services Administration. Projects may include space expansions, contractions, reconfigurations, relocations, or upgrades to various aspects of their existing space including outdated, dilapidated or insufficient elements such as furniture, security features, or audio/visual equipment. Leading coordination with OFAM subject matter experts and applicable facility owners toward resolution of any lease related issues that arise for any leased space or maintenance and repair issues not promptly addressed. Performing occupancy cost analysis, analyzing and justifying operating expenses, maintaining accurate documentation, and resolving issues efficiently. Utilizing the automated real property program TRIRIGA to take corrective actions for users, resolve data reporting errors, and identify complex existing or potential program issues to PMO leadership, while making recommendations for timely and executable plans for corrective actions.

Requiremennts

You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this position Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered with Selective Service Primary U.S. residency for at least three of the last five years (additional details below) All pre-employment processes will be conducted in English You may be required to pass a background investigation CBP follows the DHS Drug-Free Workplace Plan for drug testing procedures As an employee of CBP, you will be joining a workforce that is dedicated to accomplishing our mission while maintaining the trust of our Nation by strictly adhering to all government ethics standards. Your conduct will be subject to the ethics rules applicable to all Executive Branch employees, and to CBP employees specifically, as well as the criminal conflict of interest statutes. Once you enter on duty, these rules include obtaining approval for outside employment or business activity, to ensure such employment or business activity is not prohibited and does not interfere or conflict with performance of your official duties. Please review further details via the following link. DHS uses E-Verify, an internet-based system, to confirm the eligibility of all newly hired employees to work in the United States. Learn more about E-Verify including your rights and responsibilities. Bargaining Unit: This is a bargaining unit covered position, represented under the National Treasury Employees Unions - NTEU. For local chapter contact information see Chapter Websites - National Treasury Employees Union - NTEU The Department of Homeland Security encourages persons with disabilities to apply, to include persons with intellectual, severe physical or psychiatric disabilities, as defined by 5 CFR

213.3102(u), and/or Disabled Veterans with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more as defined by 5 CFR
315.707. Veterans, Peace Corps/VISTA volunteers, and persons with disabilities possess a wealth of unique talents, experiences, and competencies that can be invaluable to the DHS mission. If you are a member of one of these groups, you may not have to compete with the public for federal jobs. To determine your eligibility for non-competitive appointment and to understand the required documentation, click on the links above or contact the Servicing Human Resources Office listed at the bottom of this announcement.

Qualifications

Experience: You qualify for the GS-13 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Implementing and monitoring maintenance, repair, and operations programs. Performing analytical studies related to programming, budget planning, financial management, project control, acquisition of supplies and equipment logistics management, security management, staff management, and information technology support. Advising management and other stakeholders on the results and implications of strategic planning studies and analyses and making recommendations for process improvement. Measuring program and project performance, developing data-driven recommendations for improvement, and implementing new program strategies and methodologies to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. NOTE: Your resume must explicitly indicate how you meet this requirement, otherwise you will be found ineligible. Please see the "Required Documents" section below for additional resume requirements. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Background Investigation: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is a federal law enforcement agency that requires all applicants to undergo a thorough background investigation prior to employment in order to promote the agency's core values of vigilance, service to country, and integrity. During the screening and/or background investigation process, you will be asked questions regarding any felony criminal convictions or current felony charges, the use of illegal drugs (e.g., marijuana, cocaine, heroin, LSD, methamphetamines, ecstasy), and the use of non-prescribed controlled substances including any experimentation, possession, sale, receipt, manufacture, cultivation, production, transfer, shipping, trafficking, or distribution of controlled substances. jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Test Automation
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Test Automation Engineering team develops test systems used to ensure the quality and reliability of Anduril’s products. The team works on complex manufacturing test solutions for our internal manufacturing team and deploys out to contract manufacturers. We work closely and cross-functionally with the rest of our Product Engineering groups that include Electrical, Mechanical and Firmware Engineering to solve and improve our manufacturing processes, product quality and reliability.

About The Job

In this position, you will own large parts of the end-to-end test system development - enhancing transparency and generating actional reports to support strategic and tactical decision making. You’ll support increasing efficiencies throughout our end-to-end processes, all with a focus on introducing scale and resiliency into our growing people and tools footprint. If you thrive in fast-paced, technical environments and excel at juggling multiple responsibilities, we want to hear from you.

We’re looking for a Senior Program Manager to own the planning, execution, and delivery of tester solutions in the Hardware Engineering Services Department. You’ll be an ally collaborating with our partner Programs, working directly with other Program Managers, Engineering Leads, Internal/External Manufacturing, Supply Chain and Logistics.

What You'll Do

Responsible for successful program execution, exceeding both internal and external stakeholder expectations and meeting all contractual commitments
Demonstrate collaborative leadership skills by building trust with your teams, customers, and peers while holding yourself and the cross functional team accountable to execute on business outcomes
Communicate effectively and with confidence when engaging with customers and Anduril leadership
Manage the overall program schedule from kickoff planning to tester deployment, including critical path tracking, schedule risk mitigations, visibility to Anduril leadership and updates to the customer
Navigate customer change requests while maintaining program velocity and adhering to financial targets through scope management and change control
Ensure decisions support current efforts and position the company for continued hardware engineering services growth
Support Test Automation leadership in preparation and management of critical technical and business forums
Provide structure to ambiguity and help drive production stakeholders towards decisions on tactical and strategic issues
Execute creative solutions on short timelines to get answers quickly, while also considering more scalable solutions that will make Anduril successful in the long term
Analyze test program metrics to identify trends, patterns, and areas for improvement of test product processes.

Required Qualifications

5+ years experience managing the development of technical systems throughout the product lifecycle
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field (technical background preferred)
Proven track record of managing medium to large-scale, complex programs across the product development lifecycle
Demonstrated ability to create and execute a complex program schedule
Demonstrated ability to actively develop and execute an effective program risk management plan
Experience in developing and executing communication strategies for high-visibility programs
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills
Experience coordinating multiple internal and external teams within a complex engineering or technology-focused organization
Willingness to travel as needed (up to 15%)
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance.

US Salary Range

$147,000—$220,000 USD

Benefits

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind

No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

As Program Manager, Data Transformation, you will run the day-to-day program engine that turns Oura's business data into governed, trusted, decision-ready metrics. You will work inside the Data Transformation program, alongside the Staff Program Manager, and own the delivery rhythm for your assigned data domains: intake, prioritization, tracking, ownership, certification, and reporting. Early focus areas include Hardware and Supply Chain, where the need for structure is greatest.A core part of the job is metric certification and intake discipline. You will enforce the three-path model for every request and metric: Directional (fit for use, fast), Governed (executive, board, investor, or external numbers, with a certification path), and Not ours (operational or application work rerouted to the owning business team). You will also drive the work itself, including sprints where they help, so certification and delivery commitments actually land.Hardware and supply chain data, for example, spans manufacturing, quality, logistics, sourcing, planning, and new product introduction. This role connects those teams to Data Engineering and Analytics so that the numbers executives, finance, and auditors rely on (for example warranty rate, click-to-delivery, and yield) have one definition, one owner, and a clear path from directional to governed to certified.This role is ideal for a program manager who is comfortable in ambiguity, can read a data pipeline diagram as easily as a project plan, and likes bringing structure to fast-moving, cross-functional work.

What You Will Do

Take business metrics from informally tracked to fully certified, each with a locked definition, a single accountable owner, and documented lineage and controls
Make sure every key metric in your domains has a clear owner and approver, and keep that ownership current as the business changes
Triage incoming data requests by their intended use and level of rigor, and route work that belongs to other teams to the right place
Run a structured intake process with clear priorities, business justification, and reliable response times
Drive cross-functional programs to completion across Data Engineering, Finance, Supply Chain, Hardware, and IT, using agile practices where they help
Keep program plans accurate and visible, with named leads, dates, and status that stakeholders can trust
Track data issues and metric regressions through to resolution, and support documentation for internal and external audit
Communicate progress and data health clearly to senior leaders, and drive adoption of standardized metric definitions

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

What You'll Bring

5 to 8 years of experience in program management, technical program management, or business operations, including time supporting data, analytics, or operations teams
Experience running cross-functional programs with many stakeholders and competing priorities, without formal authority
Experience with metric governance or controls work: definitions, ownership, documentation, and formal sign-off
Comfortable working in Databricks or a similar lakehouse: can navigate the catalog, read a SQL query or model to understand how a metric is computed, and spot-check numbers against source tables
Working understanding of data pipelines and transformation layers (dbt or equivalent): can follow lineage from source system to reported number and explain where a metric is computed
Experience with data quality controls: defining validation tests, reading test results, and tracing failures to root cause
Comfort holding a process line with senior stakeholders, including redirecting requests, while keeping relationships intact
Hands-on experience with work tracking tools such as Jira, and with running sprints or lightweight agile cadences
Clear written and verbal communication, including status reporting for senior audiences

Nice To Have

Experience with hardware, manufacturing, quality, logistics, sourcing, or supply planning
Background in consumer hardware, wearables, medical devices, or another regulated hardware business
Exposure to financial reporting, SOX-style controls, audit preparation, or IPO readiness
Experience at a high-growth or pre-IPO company
Experience working with distributed teams across US and European time zones
Comfort using modern AI tooling to speed up analysis, documentation, and reporting

Benefits

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What We Offer

Competitive salary
Lunch benefit
Wellness benefit
Flexible working hours
Collaborative, smart teammates
An Ōura ring of your own
Wellness Time Off

While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. jobs.title: Acquisition Project Manager - Federal Acquisition Service
jobs.description:
Summary

As an Acquisition Project Manager you will lead complex, high-value Department of War or civilian agency IT and professional service acquisitions through the pre-award lifecycle, serving as the technical expert from project initiation to task order award.

Location of position:
This position is within the Federal Acquisition Service, Assisted Acquisition Services, OSO.

We are currently filling four vacancies, but additional vacancies may be filled as needed.

Learn more about this agency

Duties

Serves as an expert Acquisition Project Manager and concurrently and independently leads at least one or multiple highly-complex, high-dollar ($250M+) acquisitions from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award providing technical advice to the client, contractors, and AAS regarding pre- award strategies and activities. Identifies, analyzes, strategizes, optimally schedules, and tracks acquisition milestones to ensure that the acquisition satisfies client’s mission needs.
Assesses, defines, and documents client technical and contractual requirements which can include state of the art or unprecedented needs. Conducts market research and identifies the optimal acquisition strategy to accomplish the client requirement. Incorporates acquisition best practices to satisfy client needs. Solves complex acquisition challenges that may arise during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle.
Translates client requirements and acquisition strategy into written documentation. Prepares the solicitation and related acquisition documents in accordance with the approved acquisition strategy. Uses expert acquisition and analytical knowledge, writes technical evaluation reports summarizing the Technical Evaluation Board findings.
Develops and maintains partnerships with clients, contractor support staff, and other GSA employees. Works with the Contracting Officer to solicit competition and provide fair opportunity through industry engagement activities such as Industry Day, Reading Rooms, and Due Diligence.
Provides leadership to matrixed Integrated Project Teams during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle. Coordinates team responsibilities, manages client expectations, resolves complex acquisition issues, mentors junior staff, and ensures acquisition documentation and project files are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

US Citizenship or National (Residents of American Samoa and Swains Island)
Meet all eligibility criteria within 30 days of the closing date
Meet time-in-grade within 30 days of the closing date, if applicable
Register with Selective Service if you are a male born after 12/31/1959
Requires temporary duty business travel approximately 25% of the time.

If selected, you must meet the following conditions:

Current or Former Political Appointees: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C or Non­Career SES employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the HR Office. Failure to disclose this information could result in disciplinary action including removal from Federal Service.
Serve a one year probationary period, if required.
Undergo and pass a background investigation (Tier 2 investigation level).
Have your identity and work status eligibility verified if you are not a GSA employee. We will use the Department of Homeland Security’s e-Verify system for this. Any discrepancies must be resolved as a condition of continued employment.
Complete a financial disclosure report to verify that no conflict, or an appearance of conflict, exists between your financial interest and this position.

Qualifications

To evaluate your qualifications, your resume must clearly demonstrate how you meet the specialized experience described below.
Your resume must not exceed two pages. To ensure your qualifications can be fully evaluated, we recommend including the following information:

Name, address, telephone number, email address;
Job Title (if Federal Service, provide series and grade; if not in GS plan, provide GS equivalent grade);
Relevant work experience—should include employer name, job title, start and end dates (month/year), the number of hours worked per week and descriptions that explain how you meet the required qualifications in the job announcement.
Education, certifications or licensures—If the job announcement requires any education, certifications or licensures, make sure to include the required information and any required documents like transcripts.

Your resume should contain enough information to make a valid determination that you fully meet experience requirements for each grade level you are applying to. If you do not provide enough information for us to determine your qualifications, you may be rated ineligible.

If you have volunteered your service through a National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, Americorps), we encourage you to apply and include this experience on your resume.

The GS-13
salary range starts at $106,437per year. If you are a new federal employee, your starting salary will likely be set at the Step 1 of the grade for which you are selected.

To qualify, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or higher in the Federal service. Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated expertise in Federal acquisition and project management, specifically from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award. Such experience must include:

Providing technical advice; identifying and developing customer agency requirements;
Preparing and documenting the acquisition strategy;
Preparing statements of work and/or performance work statements;
Determining contract type; and
Leading the technical evaluation of proposals.

Additional information

Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin.

Applicants are encouraged to make their resume searchable in their USAJOBS.gov profile. This will allow Federal hiring specialists and hiring managers across agencies to find their resume as part of agency recruitment campaigns or staffing searches.

If you apply to this position and are selected, we will not ask about your criminal history before you receive a conditional job offer. If you believe you were asked about your criminal history improperly, contact the agency or visit GSA's webpage.

Additional vacancies may be filled through this announcement in this or other GSA organizations within the same commuting area as needed; through other means; or not at all.

Relocation-related expenses are not approved and will be your responsibility.

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.

Benefits

A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. Opens in a new windowLearn more about federal benefits.

You will have access to many benefits including:

Health insurance (choose from a wide range of plans)
Life insurance coverage with several options
Sick leave and vacation time, including 11 paid holidays per year
Thrift Savings Plan (similar to a 401(k) plan)
Transit and child care subsidies
Flexible spending accounts
Long-term care insurance
Training and development

Eligibility for benefits depends on the type of position you hold and whether your position is full-time, part-time or intermittent. Contact the hiring agency for more information on the specific benefits offered.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Project Manager for our Power Constructors, Inc. (PCI) sector. Your home office would be either in Tampa or Orlando, Florida; however, this position can be remote. Be involved in projects with our P&E team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our clients’ objectives and solves their challenges.

This position will have the ability to work remotely from anywhere in the United States. WSP will not provide sponsorship for this position.

WSP brings global expertise in power delivery, power generation, and program management—anchored by the acquisition of POWER Engineers, Inc. TRC Companies have now joined WSP, deepening our power practice and expanding our energy advisory and intelligent grid services. We're partnering with clients to shape how energy systems evolve around the world—and we need your help.

This Opportunity

Oversees the planning and execution of large-scale, technically complex construction projects by providing strategic direction, resolving high-impact field issues, and ensuring alignment with client expectations, contract requirements, and performance objectives. Leverages deep expertise in construction methods, regulatory compliance, and contract administration to lead multidisciplinary teams and deliver high-quality project outcomes. Supports the development of long-term project strategies, promotes innovation in construction practices, and champions risk mitigation efforts that preserve schedule, cost, and safety performance. Acts as a trusted advisor to clients and internal leadership while mentoring team members and contributing to organizational excellence in construction delivery.

Your Impact

Coordinating construction activities within substations throughout all Districts to facilitate Distribution Automation.
Document control for engineered communication one-line drawings, site visit notes, and construction task requests.
Maintain Project status log for all Distribution Automation and Under Frequency Design projects, communicate project details and updates to internal and external stakeholders.
Submit weekly and bi-weekly reports to internal and external stakeholders.
Maintain lines of communication between different stakeholders including Protection and Control technicians, Field Construction Coordinators, Telecommunication technicians, and Engineer’s
Lead overall field execution and construction oversight for complex projects or large multi-site programs.
Coordinate technical and operational aspects of construction, ensuring alignment with engineering design, contract scope, and regulatory standards.
Resolve escalated technical, logistical, and constructability issues in coordination with project stakeholders.
Serve as the senior field liaison between clients, contractors, consultants, and agency representatives.
Oversee the implementation of construction safety strategies and promote a culture of safety excellence.
Lead the review of detailed project schedules, assess critical path elements, and guide schedule recovery efforts.
Provide high-level input to contract negotiations, change order evaluations, and dispute resolution processes.
Support QA/QC implementation across the project lifecycle, including review of inspection reports and corrective actions.
Champion constructability and risk reviews, offering innovative solutions to optimize construction delivery.
Participate in executive-level client briefings, board meetings, and progress reporting forums.
Develop and implement field execution plans that align with project goals and resource availability.
Guide the integration of project controls with field data to improve reporting accuracy and decision-making.
Ensure compliance with applicable environmental regulations, site permits, and sustainability requirements.
Contribute to the preparation of claims defense documentation and forensic construction analyses.
Lead technical mentoring and training of junior and mid-level staff, supporting workforce development.
Drive the coordination of punch list development, final inspections, and system commissioning.
Collaborate with design teams to review constructability concerns and implement design modifications.
Support preconstruction and proposal efforts by developing field strategies, logistics plans, and staffing projections.
Evaluate contractor performance and participate in performance reviews and closeout assessments.
Contribute to innovation initiatives by promoting new tools, technologies, and process improvements.
Lead lessons learned efforts and disseminate findings across the construction management practice.
Provide expert-level technical input to organizational best practices, standards, and construction delivery frameworks.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources, and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in construction management or closely related discipline, or demonstrated proven equivalent experience.
10+ years of relevant post-education experience in construction management or related areas.
Extensive experience managing field execution on large, complex infrastructure or vertical construction projects.
Proven expertise in construction methodologies, phasing strategies, and site coordination techniques.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage multidisciplinary teams and coordinate multiple workstreams.
Experience negotiating, executing, and managing construction contracts and associated change orders.
Expert knowledge of critical path scheduling, delay analysis, and schedule risk management.
Demonstrated ability to resolve highly complex field challenges and technical disputes.
Strong understanding of federal, state, and local permitting and environmental compliance requirements.
Experience with QA/QC programs, inspection processes, and regulatory documentation.
Advanced knowledge of OSHA and site safety practices with the ability to guide implementation.
Proficiency in construction management platforms (e.g., Procore, Bluebeam, Autodesk Construction Cloud).
Ability to prepare and present executive-level progress reports, technical documentation, and briefings.
Familiarity with earned value management and integration of cost and schedule data.
Track record of success supporting or leading claims resolution, forensic analyses, and audit readiness.
Demonstrated experience in developing field logistics and access plans for high-traffic or constrained sites.
Commitment to mentorship and ability to develop technical talent within project teams.
Ability to communicate effectively with senior leadership, clients, and contractors under high-pressure situations.
Capable of working across offices and geographic regions to support distributed project delivery.
Understanding of contract risk allocation, liability clauses, and project insurance frameworks.
Experience in project closeout, turnover planning, and lifecycle asset integration.
Record of ethical leadership, client stewardship, and operational excellence.
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Demonstrated history of delivering technically challenging projects on time and within budget.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree
Certified Construction Manager (CCM) or equivalent credential.
Essential project management certification required (e.g., PMP, CAP-M).
OSHA 30-hour certification or equivalent health and safety training.

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Project Manager based in Canada.

Are you an experienced project management professional passionate about delivering complex technology implementations and building lasting client relationships? This fully remote, full-time opportunity allows you to lead end-to-end ERP implementation projects for clients in the food and beverage industry. You will take ownership of project delivery, ensuring timelines, budgets, and scope remain on track while maintaining high levels of client satisfaction. Beyond managing projects, you will play a strategic role in strengthening client partnerships, identifying business growth opportunities, and minimizing delivery risks. You will also mentor project managers, establish best practices, and help improve processes across a growing, technology-driven organization. This role is ideal for a proactive leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys solving complex challenges, and wants to make a meaningful impact on both client success and team performance.

Accountabilities

End-to-end project delivery: Lead ERP and SaaS implementation projects from planning through execution and completion, ensuring deliverables meet agreed timelines, budgets, scope, and quality expectations.
Client relationship management: Build and maintain strong, long-term client relationships that support customer satisfaction, retention, profitability, and strategic business objectives.
Client expectations and issue resolution: Communicate proactively with clients, address concerns independently, navigate difficult conversations, resolve issues, and minimize escalations while maintaining trust and confidence.
Business development and upselling: Identify opportunities to expand client engagements, recommend additional services where appropriate, and strengthen relationships with customers who can serve as long-term references.
Plan-driven execution: Use project plans as the primary reference for activities, milestones, responsibilities, and timelines, ensuring assigned resources remain accountable for their deliverables and provide accurate progress updates.
Risk management: Identify potential project risks, budget overruns, delays, and deviations early, implement corrective measures, and escalate issues appropriately when required.
Financial and scope management: Maintain accurate, up-to-date project budgets and scope documentation, anticipate financial risks, manage change orders, and coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure commercial alignment.
Stakeholder communication: Provide timely, clear, and consistent updates to clients, internal teams, and leadership regarding project progress, risks, financial performance, and outstanding actions.
Independent ownership: Proactively drive workstreams forward, anticipate project needs, follow through on commitments, and ensure open items are resolved without requiring constant supervision.
Team leadership and mentorship: Coach and mentor other project managers, share knowledge, support onboarding, and help colleagues strengthen their project delivery capabilities.
Process improvement: Lead internal initiatives to improve project management standards, documentation, tools, workflows, and delivery practices across the organization.
Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with implementation specialists, technical teams, and other stakeholders to resolve challenges, coordinate resources, and deliver successful client outcomes.
On-site client engagement: Travel to client facilities when required, including food production and processing environments, to support project implementation, understand operational requirements, and facilitate effective delivery.

Requirements

Education: Degree in Business, Accounting, Finance, Management Information Systems (MIS), or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Project management experience: Demonstrated success delivering ERP or SaaS implementation projects, including complex implementations involving multiple stakeholders, technical requirements, and operational dependencies.
Proven delivery track record: Experience successfully managing at least 10 projects with budgets exceeding CAD $100,000 each, covering the full project lifecycle from planning and execution to financial management and delivery.
Complex project management: Experience with complex ERP implementations or construction projects is required. Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously is a strong asset.
Client relationship expertise: Strong experience managing client expectations, resolving issues independently, handling sensitive conversations, and preventing escalations through proactive communication and problem-solving.
Financial accountability: Proven ability to manage project budgets, anticipate financial risks, oversee change orders, maintain accurate financial reporting, and align commercial decisions with internal stakeholders.
Structured execution: Demonstrated ability to manage projects according to detailed plans, maintain accountability for milestones, identify deviations early, and implement corrective actions.
Leadership and mentorship: Experience coaching other project managers, improving team performance, and introducing tools, processes, and standards that enhance project delivery.
Communication and interpersonal skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to lead client meetings, communicate complex issues clearly, and collaborate effectively across teams.
Organization and adaptability: Strong prioritization, multitasking, and time-management skills, with the ability to manage competing demands and perform effectively in high-pressure situations.
Self-motivation and ownership: A proactive, results-oriented mindset, with the ability to work independently, anticipate needs, take initiative, and follow through on commitments.
Technology awareness: Familiarity with current technology trends and AI-powered tools. Hands-on experience with Claude is considered an asset.
Travel readiness: Willingness and ability to travel approximately 15–20% of the time and maintain a valid passport.
On-site environment requirements: Ability and willingness to access food production and client facilities that may involve prolonged standing or walking, loud noises, bright or flashing lights, stairs and ladders, and the use of protective or sanitary equipment such as hairnets, gloves, boots, shoe covers, lab coats, or coveralls.
Operational and safety awareness: Comfort working near food products, including raw meat and/or live animals, and the ability to recognize and respond appropriately to visual and auditory safety signals.

Benefits

Competitive annual salary: CAD $120,000–$150,000, based on experience, qualifications, and relevant expertise.
Performance-based compensation: Opportunity to earn additional compensation through a bonus program.
Fully remote work: Flexibility to work remotely from Canada, with travel required for client engagements.
Paid time off: Annual paid leave to support rest, personal commitments, and work-life balance.
Comprehensive health coverage: Medical and dental insurance plans.
Financial protection: Life and disability insurance coverage.
Immediate benefits eligibility: No waiting period before benefits coverage begins.
Retirement savings: Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) to support long-term financial planning.
Leadership opportunities: Take ownership of high-value implementation projects while mentoring colleagues and influencing team-wide delivery standards.
Professional development: Opportunities to strengthen expertise in ERP implementation, project leadership, client management, and emerging AI-enabled tools.
Collaborative, technology-driven environment: Work with a knowledgeable, multidisciplinary team in a growing organization that values initiative, accountability, teamwork, and customer success.
Meaningful client impact: Help food and beverage businesses improve operations through technology solutions tailored to their industry-specific needs.

Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

Job Description

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) is seeking a highly experienced Principal Program Manager to lead Catalyst and Learning and Development programming for OCI Data Centers across Japan and Asia Pacific (JAPAC) and Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA).

In this role, you will own the strategy, implementation, regional expansion, and ongoing management of scalable talent-development programs for OCI Data Center employees. Your portfolio will include Catalyst, an early-career onboarding and development program for employees entering data center roles with limited or no prior industry experience, as well as broader learning and development initiatives. Catalyst also encompasses onboarding and development for military talent.

You will establish a consistent global program foundation while adapting delivery to meet regional, cultural, language, operational, and business needs across JAPAC and EMEA. You will partner closely with Data Center Operations, regional and site leaders, Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, subject-matter experts, while sitting in the centralized Data Center Onboarding & Development organization, with peer Learning & Development instructional designers, training delivery experts, and program managers.

The ideal candidate has a proven track record of building and scaling early-career, onboarding, learning and development, or train-the-trainer programs across multiple countries or business units. You are comfortable operating in a fast-moving and ambiguous environment, influencing stakeholders at all levels, and translating business requirements into repeatable programs that improve employee readiness, development, and time to productivity. You communicate clearly, use data to guide decisions, and demonstrate an “act now and iterate” mindset.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
Five or more years of relevant experience in program management, learning and development, talent development, Human Resources, workforce development, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience launching, managing, and improving complex programs at scale.
Experience developing or managing early-career, onboarding, learning and development, or train-the-trainer programs.
Experience leading cross-functional initiatives involving business leaders, operational teams, Human Resources, Talent Acquisition, and other partner organizations.
Exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, including experience communicating with operational, business, technical, and senior leadership audiences.
Proven track record of taking ownership, identifying solutions, and driving work to completion.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Ability to collaborate effectively across countries, cultures, and time zones within JAPAC and EMEA.
Willingness to travel periodically to OCI Data Center locations and regional meetings, as business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing programs across multiple countries or regions, particularly within JAPAC or EMEA.
Experience supporting technical, engineering, operations, infrastructure, or data center workforces.
Experience with cloud infrastructure services or large-scale technology operations.
Experience building and maintaining internal trainer, facilitator, or learning-champion networks.
Experience adapting global programs for regional, cultural, language, or operational requirements.
Ability to think broadly and strategically while maintaining strong attention to execution and operational detail.
Experience presenting program insights and recommendations to senior leaders.

Responsibilities

Program Strategy and Ownership

Own the end-to-end implementation, governance, and continuous improvement of Catalyst and related learning and development programs across JAPAC and EMEA, while partnering with the AMER Catalyst Program owner to create global consistency.
Create a consistent core program model while identifying where regional or site-level customization is necessary.
Establish program roadmaps, implementation plans, success criteria, and mechanisms for monitoring progress, risks, dependencies, and outcomes.
Lead the regional implementation and expansion of Catalyst programming for employees entering OCI Data Center roles with limited or no relevant industry experience.

Learning and Development Programming

Build and manage scalable learning and development programs that support onboarding, workforce readiness, and ongoing capability development across OCI Data Center sites.
Own the implementation of the Trainer Accreditation Program across JAPAC and EMEA.
Establish and maintain a regional network of qualified internal trainers and facilitators with sufficient coverage to support recurring hiring and learning needs.
Partner with subject-matter experts and learning professionals to ensure training is accurate, relevant, accessible, and aligned with operational requirements.

Regional Expansion and Localization

Develop expansion plans for introducing Catalyst and L&D programming at existing and new OCI Data Center locations across JAPAC and EMEA.
Translate global program standards into practical regional delivery models that account for local operating environments, languages, cultures, and workforce needs.
Identify regional constraints and dependencies early and develop solutions that preserve program quality while supporting local requirements.
Capture lessons learned and create reusable playbooks, templates, and tools that accelerate future program launches.

Stakeholder Leadership

Build trusted relationships with stakeholders ranging from front-line managers and site leaders to senior leaders across OCI, Human Resources, Talent Acquisition.
Facilitate alignment across geographically dispersed teams with different priorities, requirements, and operating models.
Provide clear, timely updates on program status, decisions, risks, dependencies, and results.
Serve as a subject-matter expert and strategic advisor on early-career onboarding, trainer enablement, and scalable Data Center learning programs.

Measurement and Continuous Improvement

Define and monitor program performance indicators, including participation, completion, learner experience, trainer readiness, program capacity, proficiency, and time to productivity.
Use quantitative and qualitative data to identify trends, assess program effectiveness, and recommend improvements.
Establish regular business-review mechanisms and present program results, risks, and recommendations to regional and global leaders.
Continuously improve program processes, content, tools, and delivery methods based on business results and stakeholder feedback.

Qualifications

Career Level - IC5

About Us

Only Oracle brings together the data, infrastructure, applications, and expertise to power everything from industry innovations to life-saving care. And with AI embedded across our products and services, we help customers turn that promise into a better future for all. Discover your potential at a company leading the way in AI and cloud solutions that impact billions of lives.

True innovation starts when everyone is empowered to contribute. Program Manager - Data Center and Cloud

GDIT is seeking a Program Manager - Data Center and Cloud for the Federal Civilian Division to join our outstanding team! You will lead a large scale, global Data Center and Cloud Services contract supporting the U.S. Department of State’s Bureau of Diplomatic Technology (DT). The role oversees 24x7x365 operations across geographically dispersed data centers and FEDRAMP-authorized public/private cloud environments, driving mission uptime, security, performance, and modernization aligned to DOS objectives.

Responsibilities include contract performance, people leadership, innovation, quality, and mission. Success requires experiencing leading large, diverse teams across multiple time zones, data-driven and transparent reporting, and customer collaboration.

HOW A PROGRAM MANAGER - DATA CENTER AND CLOUD WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

Strategic Leadership & Program Management:

Lead the end-to-end delivery of Platform Engineering Support Services, including Converged Infrastructure/Cloud Engineering, Network Engineering, Data Protection, Monitoring, Security Infrastructure, Procurement Support, New Product/Service Development, and Special Projects.
Translate DOS mission, policy, and regulatory requirements into actionable roadmaps and measurable outcomes; standardize and streamline processes to reduce delivery time and cost while improving alignment between mission and IT.
Build and mentor a multidisciplinary workforce across multiple sites and shifts; champion knowledge transfer to Government FTE counterparts and support contractors.
Establish transparent governance, reporting, and stakeholder engagement.

Operations & Service Delivery:

Direct 24x7x365 enterprise data center and cloud operations ensuring availability, proactive monitoring, and rapid incident/problem resolution.
Enforce ITIL-aligned service management and manage SLAs, SLOs, KPIs, MTTR, and performance trending.
Oversee capacity and performance management to sustain CPU/memory/storage allocation and prevent over-provisioning; drive automation for patching, compliance, and configuration baselines.
Coordinate Enterprise Operations and distributed Site Operations across multiple data centers.

Security, Compliance & Risk Management:

Ensure continuous compliance with federal cybersecurity frameworks and DOS directives; support ATO and continuous monitoring activities.
Lead risk management, resilience/COOP/DR planning, and audit response; integrate security posture reporting into operational dashboards.
Support FedRAMP compliance and associated cloud security requirements.

Financial & Resource Management:

Own program financials, staffing strategies, subcontractor oversight, and performance to cost/schedule baselines.
Drive workforce development, retention, ethics, compliance, and succession planning.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Cybersecurity, a related technical discipline or business required (master’s preferred).
Experience: 10+ years of years managing complex IT or network programs, including global environments.
Work Experience: 10+ years experience managing complex IT or network programs, including global environments, leading large, diverse teams and demonstrated experience delivering large scale data center and infrastructure modernization and cloud migration initiatives.
Certification: Project Management Professional (PMP), ITIL v4 or v5 Intermediate (Specialist or higher) level certification or equivalent
Technical skills: Expertise in emerging technologies including, but not limited to AI, Digital Modernization, DevSecOps, Cloud, and Cyber. Demonstrated success leading large, diverse, multi-site teams supporting 24x7x365 operations. Proven experience with hybrid cloud (public/private/FEDRAMP), enterprise data centers, and ITIL processes.
Security clearance level: Active Top Secret level clearance
Location: Hybrid to multiple locations throughout the National Capital Region (at least 3 days/week in office); Local travel to customer and industry locations is expected and some travel outside of the area

At GDIT, the mission is our purpose, and our people are at the center of everything we do.

new_jobs.description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

The Role

We are seeking a Senior Program Manager, Customer Program Management - Data Center GPU to lead key AI platform and customer programs from concept through production deployment. The role will focus primarily on OEM/ODM partners and enterprise customers, driving end-to-end execution across platform development, system validation, cluster bring-up, performance optimization, and production ramp.

Working across hardware, firmware, software, systems engineering, product management, support, business development, sales, and go-to-market teams, you will translate customer and product objectives into executable plans. You will serve as a primary program point of contact internally and externally, ensuring milestones are achieved and technical issues are resolved.

The Person

The ideal candidate combines strong technical program management experience with practical knowledge of complex data center GPU, server, and software systems. They are highly organized, technically credible, and comfortable leading horizontally across globally distributed engineering, business, OEM/ODM partner, and enterprise customer teams.

The successful candidate can clarify and analyze technical requirements, build integrated program plans across hardware and software dependencies, drive accountability, anticipate execution risks, and communicate status, decisions, and mitigation plans clearly to technical and business leadership. Experience supporting OEM/ODM partners and enterprise or large-scale AI customers through platform development, validation, cluster deployment, optimization, and production ramp is highly valued.

Key Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end customer and product programs for data center GPU platforms, from requirements and technical feasibility through development, validation, deployment, and production ramp.
Translate customer requirements and senior technical guidance into clear program scope, schedules, milestones, KPIs, dependencies, deliverables, and ownership.
Coordinate hardware, firmware, driver, software stack, system validation, support, product, and customer teams to achieve program milestones and release objectives.
Develop integrated schedules that account for hardware, firmware, driver, software, platform, validation, and customer-environment dependencies; negotiate plans that support overall program commitments.
Support OEM/ODM and enterprise customer engagements through proof-of-concept, platform development, system validation, cluster bring-up, performance tuning, production deployment, and ongoing readiness at scale.
Communicate program status, decisions, issues, risks, and recommended mitigation plans to cross-functional teams, customers, partners, and leadership.
Drive timely resolution of technical and execution roadblocks through structured issue management, clear accountability, and appropriate escalation.
Partner with Product Management and Engineering to capture customer requirements and provide actionable feedback on hardware, firmware, driver, and software priorities.
Build and maintain well-developed program plans, risk assessments, dependency tracking, reporting mechanisms, and decision frameworks throughout the program lifecycle.
Identify opportunities to improve deployment processes, validation methodologies, release coordination, system reliability, and overall customer program execution.
Plan proactively for development and deployment risks, identify prevention and mitigation methods, and address issues early to reduce schedule disruption and engineering cost.

Preferred Experience

Proven program management experience in a dynamic, competitive technology environment, particularly within software development, systems engineering, or hardware engineering organizations.
Experience supporting data center GPUs, accelerators, servers, AI infrastructure, or other complex compute platforms.
Experience working directly with OEM/ODM partners, system integrators, enterprise data center customers, or large-scale AI customers.
Understanding of data center infrastructure, server architectures, Linux environments, GPU software stacks, and large-scale compute deployments.
Familiarity with GPU software ecosystems such as ROCm, including drivers, firmware, containerized environments, software releases, and performance optimization.
Experience managing programs involving platform validation, system debug, post-silicon activities, cluster bring-up, software release coordination, and production ramp.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex schedules, cross-functional dependencies, risks, KPIs, and deliverables across multiple organizations.
Strong customer-facing verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical issues into clear program status, risks, decisions, and actions.
Proven horizontal leadership and ability to lead within a matrixed organization across globally distributed teams, with flexibility to support execution across Asia and North America.
Background in technical program management, systems engineering, customer engineering, customer success, or technical account management within data center environments.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field; master's or other advanced degree preferred.

new_jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own program execution for cloud availability — the maintenance windows, host patching, network switch upgrades, and incident management work that keeps our GPU infrastructure running reliably for customers. This role sits with an engineering team that manages system uptime and infrastructure SLAs and has not historically worked with a TPM function, so the right candidate earns credibility through technical depth and execution rigor rather than process alone. You'll drive planning and execution of maintenance windows that balance minimal customer disruption against critical hardware and firmware updates, coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents, and build the lightweight frameworks that bring predictability to an operationally complex environment. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants to be personally in the room for incident calls and switch upgrade planning, not managing from a dashboard

What You’ll Be Working On:

Maintenance Window Planning & Execution: Own the planning and execution of maintenance windows/production changes for high-availability cloud infrastructure, balancing minimal customer workload disruption against the need for host patching and hardware updates.
Incident Management: Coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents or unplanned outages — driving communications, leading post-incident reviews (PIRs), and tracking remediation items through to closure without compromising SLA commitments.
Network Switch Upgrades: Support planning for major network switch upgrades and migrations, tracking the hardest dependencies and flagging what's most likely to break before it does.
Technical Risk Identification: Catch technical risks in cloud availability programs before the engineering team surfaces them, and know when to solve it directly versus escalate.
Vendor & Partner Coordination: Engage directly with hardware/network vendors and Customer Success on high-stakes infrastructure upgrades, keeping customer-facing teams informed through the process.
Program Frameworks: Build lightweight, fit-for-purpose execution frameworks for well-scoped availability and reliability programs (e.g., firmware update campaigns) where none exist today.
AI-Driven Program Execution: Actively use AI tools to improve risk identification, dependency tracking, and status communication in daily program work.
Engineering Credibility: Build trust with an engineering team that hasn't previously worked with a TPM — through technical fluency in maintenance workflows and incident processes, not through imposed process

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
2 to 5+ years of experience as a Technical Program Manager, with direct exposure to cloud infrastructure, availability, or operations environments.
Working knowledge of maintenance window planning, host patching, and hardware/firmware update cycles for high-availability systems.
Experience with incident management practices: cross-functional incident coordination, post-incident reviews, and remediation tracking against SLA commitments.
Familiarity with network switch upgrade or migration planning, including how to identify and track critical dependencies.
Demonstrated ability to build basic, lightweight program processes for well-defined initiatives and to know when to escalate versus solve directly.
Active use of AI tools in program management work (risk detection, status reporting, dependency mapping), with concrete examples.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for coordinating incident response and reporting status across technical and customer-facing stakeholders

Bonus Points:

Direct experience in GPU or accelerated-computing cloud infrastructure environments.
Prior experience partnering with Customer Success or customer-facing teams during infrastructure upgrades.
Exposure to designing incident management or maintenance window frameworks from scratch, rather than operating within an existing one.
Experience navigating pushback from senior technical leaders without formal authority.

The Program Manager will serve as the primary point of contact for customers, stakeholders, and internal leadership, ensuring all program objectives are met on time, within scope, and within budget. Oversee all programs and task orders on the contract, including ECP development, vehicle integration, prototyping, system design, modeling and simulation, and logistics support

Anticipate and respond to evolving customer needs, ensuring high levels of customer satisfaction

Team Leadership & Management

Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing, cross-functional program team including systems engineers, vehicle designers, integration technicians, logisticians, subcontractors, and support personnel
