Bachelor’s degree in finance or accounting
Experience in business intelligence, sales or growth operations, commercial reporting, CRM analysis or pipeline management.
Strong data-analysis capability with advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Experience maintaining data quality and producing dashboards, KPIs and management information.
Experience working with CRM systems and applying consistent data definitions or governance controls.
Experience using Salesforce and Power BI or comparable CRM and visualization tools.
Experience within business development, growth, commercial or finance function.
Experience supporting portfolio reviews, win/loss analysis or recompete reporting.

Understanding of opportunity lifecycles, pipeline governance and forecasting.

Strong attention to detail, organization and follow-through.

Pipeline data completeness, accuracy, currency and governance compliance.

Quality of prioritization, conversion, portfolio and risk analysis.

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Project Manager (Enterprise Modernization & AI Delivery
new_jobs.description:
About Tessera Labs

Tessera is an AI-native platform for enterprise transformation. The multi-agent platform delivers governed execution across ERP, CRM, HCM, and finance systems, cutting timelines from years to weeks and costs by more than half. Built on deep expertise across Oracle, SAP, Salesforce, Workday, and other systems of record, Tessera address the scope a system integrator would have traditionally taken up with the speed of execution and efficiency of an AI-native platform.

For decades, enterprises have struggled with fragmented business systems, where migrations have consumed hundreds of millions of dollars, data stayed inconsistent and unreliable, and business processes slowed under manual review. Tessera was founded to change that, for SAP and every other system enterprises depend on. The name itself — a tessera, a single tile in a mosaic — reflects our mission: unifying the disparate pieces of the enterprise into a coherent whole. Tessera is an AI-powered, multi-agent platform that harmonizes systems and lets teams work in plain English.

Our mission: Modernize global enterprises safely, automatically, and at unprecedented speed. We move fast, own outcomes end-to-end, and build at the frontier of applied AI for large-scale transformation.

Role Summary

We are seeking a Technical Project Manager (TPM) with deep expertise in delivery and value stream management to lead our most strategic customer implementations. In this role, you are not just a project scheduler. You are the delivery leader who directs cross-functional pods across multiple parallel workstreams, making sure Tessera’s multi-agent AI solutions are integrated predictably, safely, and successfully into complex enterprise environments, and that every phase of the engagement delivers measurable value.

You will be the bridge between Tessera and enterprise client’s delivery team spanning core business systems, ERP, CRM, finance, HR, and operational platforms. The role calls for strong technical fluency across enterprise architectures, business processes, integrations, and transformation programs.

You will work closely with customer Solution Architects, technical teams, system owners, and business stakeholders, translating operational and technical requirements into actionable plans for Tessera’s delivery pods. You will use your understanding of enterprise modernization to guide issue resolution, support architecture discussions, and keep every workstream aligned on what is required, technically feasible, and most valuable to the customer.

The ideal candidate has spent years leading delivery within System Integrator environments or large enterprises and wants to apply AI to accelerate modernization at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Cross-Functional Delivery Pod Leadership

Lead cross-functional delivery pods of Forward-Deployed Engineers, Data Engineers, and AI engineering teams, setting priorities, removing blockers, and holding the team accountable to outcomes
Own end-to-end delivery of multi-agent AI modernization programs from discovery through deployment and operational handoff
Build pod structures, cadences, and operating rhythms that scale across multiple concurrent customer engagements
Anticipate technical friction points related to data structures, legacy customizations, integrations, and workflow orchestration before they affect the pod’s velocity

Multi-Workstream Orchestration

Run multiple parallel workstreams across data, integration, AI agent configuration, testing, and business process alignment, managing dependencies and sequencing between them
Coordinate across Tessera teams, customer stakeholders, and third-party vendors to maintain delivery momentum across every workstream
Develop integrated program plans that give leadership a single view of progress, risk, and value across all workstreams
Support modernization efforts spanning core business systems, CRM, finance, HRIS, and operational platforms

Delivery & Value Stream Management

Map customer value streams end to end, identifying where Tessera’s agentic AI capabilities remove manual effort, shorten cycle times, and reduce cost
Define and track delivery and value metrics such as time-to-value, throughput, cycle time, and business outcomes achieved, and report them to executive stakeholders
Prioritize work by business value, so the highest-impact capabilities reach customers first
Continuously improve delivery flow by identifying bottlenecks, handoff delays, and waste across the program

Technical Communication & Stakeholder Alignment

Act as the primary technical interpreter between customer technical teams, business stakeholders, and Tessera’s AI and product organizations
Lead discovery workshops to map system landscapes, business processes, data flows, and integration points to Tessera’s agentic AI capabilities
Translate technical trade-offs, delivery plans, and value outcomes for both executive stakeholders and delivery teams
Facilitate alignment across enterprise architecture, IT operations, security, and business functions

Execution in Complex Enterprise Landscapes

Drive Agile delivery within enterprise change management frameworks and modernization methodologies
Anticipate risks related to legacy system remediation, data harmonization, integration dependencies, and business continuity
Develop mitigation plans grounded in operational and technical realities

Enterprise-Grade Governance & Deployment

Ensure all delivery activities meet enterprise standards for security, compliance, auditability, and operational governance
Oversee technical prerequisites for integrations across enterprise platforms and cloud environments
Partner with customer security and infrastructure teams to ensure successful deployments and operational readiness

Customer Engagement & Escalation Management

Serve as the primary delivery contact during onboarding and implementation
Manage technical escalations from customer IT and business teams, coordinating responses across pods, engineering, and product
Build trusted relationships with enterprise customers through clear communication, accountability, and consistent delivery

Startup Mindset & Extreme Ownership

Operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with evolving priorities and ambiguous challenges
Bring structure, clarity, and momentum to complex enterprise transformation programs
Travel to customer sites for workshops, solution design sessions, and implementation oversight as needed

Required Qualifications

4–6+ years of experience leading technical delivery for large enterprise modernization or transformation programs
Proven track record leading cross-functional delivery teams or pods through complex, technically demanding implementations
Demonstrated experience running multiple concurrent workstreams with significant dependencies
Experience mapping and managing value streams, and tying delivery work to measurable business outcomes
Comfort defining, tracking, and reporting delivery and value metrics to executive audiences
Strong understanding of enterprise business systems, integrations, data flows, and modernization challenges
Experience with one or more enterprise platforms such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics, Infor, or similar
Familiarity with enterprise architecture concepts, APIs, middleware, and cross-platform integrations
Ability to explain technical concepts, system constraints, integration challenges, and data models to both engineering teams and business stakeholders
Strong executive presence and stakeholder management skills
Strong command of Agile methodologies and experience orchestrating complex programs with multiple dependencies

Preferred Qualifications

Experience at a top-tier consulting or system integration firm (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, PwC, EY, IBM, Capgemini), or leading large enterprise modernization programs internally
Experience delivering AI/ML-enabled programs, or strong interest in LLMs, automation, and multi-agent AI orchestration
Familiarity integrating ERP and other core systems with adjacent platforms including CRM, HRIS, finance, analytics, middleware, and cloud infrastructure
PMP, Scrum Master, SAFe, value stream management, enterprise platform certifications, or related certifications are a plus

Behavioral & Problem-Solving Expectations

Balance technical systems understanding with program structure and executive communication
Lead pods with clarity, accountability, and a bias toward outcomes over activity
Operate with extreme ownership and thrive in ambiguity
Simplify complexity and drive alignment across technical and business teams
Keep a strong customer-first, value-first mindset throughout complex transformation programs

new_jobs.description:
1168381_RR00126566 Job ID: 1168381_RR00126566

NYU Grossman School of Medicine is one of the nation's top-ranked medical schools. For 175 years, NYU Grossman School of Medicine has trained thousands of physicians and scientists who have helped to shape the course of medical history and enrich the lives of countless people. An integral part of NYU Langone Health, the Grossman School of Medicine at its core is committed to improving the human condition through medical education, scientific research, and direct patient care. At NYU Langone Health, equity and inclusion are fundamental values. We strive to be a place where our exceptionally talented faculty, staff, and students of all identities can thrive. We embrace inclusion and individual skills, ideas, and knowledge.

For more information, go to med.nyu.edu , and interact with us on LinkedIn , Glassdoor , Indeed , Facebook , X and Instagram .

Position Summary

We have an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Program Manager.

This position is responsible for overseeing and managing the administrative operations of the Emergency Medicine residency training program within the NYU Grossman School of Medicine. Under the oversight of the Residency Program Director, the position reports to the Assistant Director for Education Administration with a dotted line report to the Business Manager, and supervises all of the daily responsibilities for the Emergency Medicine Residency Program Coordinator.

Job Responsibilities

Administrative
Serve as the primary administrative partner to the Residency Program Director, overseeing the coordination of program operations and facilitating effective communication and collaboration among residents, program leadership, program coordinators, faculty, Vice Chairs, and the Department Chair.
Actively participate in departmental, institutional, and education-related meetings, committees, and initiatives as assigned. Contribute to planning, decision-making, and implementation of departmental and educational priorities, and assume additional responsibilities and special projects as directed by the Assistant Director of Education, Department Administrator, Department Chair, Vice Chair of Education, and Program Directors.
Serve as a key liaison between residents, faculty, and program leadership, facilitating communication, addressing programmatic needs, and ensuring appropriate follow-up and resolution of issues.
Serve as the primary administrative liaison between the residency program and the GME Office, coordinating program requirements, communications, submissions, and institutional processes and ensuring timely follow-through on outstanding items.
Ensure residents are compliant with current documentation for licensing and institutional requirements. Verify accuracy of statistics used for reporting to FREIDA, AMA and National Resident Matching Program (NRMP).
Oversee and continuously optimize the resident onboarding process, ensuring the successful and timely integration of incoming residents and compliance with departmental, institutional, GME, and participating site requirements. Responsibilities include:
Oversee the development and maintenance of the annual resident block schedule, ensuring efficient rotation and resource allocation to support program objectives, and Balance of Trade requirements are met. Oversee resident payroll and benefits administration and coordinate the credentialing and onboarding process for incoming residents across

participating hospitals, ensuring completion of site-specific and regulatory requirements.

ii.Oversee enrollment and completion of required institutional and program-specific training, modules, systems access, and other onboarding requirements.

iii. Coordinate and help lead new resident orientation, collaborating with program leadership to develop orientation content, communicate program expectations and resources, and support residents successful transition into the program.

Oversee the resident moonlighting and Extra Work for Extra Pay processes, ensuring appropriate review, approval, submission, and tracking of applications in accordance with GME, institutional, and program requirements. Review requests and relevant program considerations and provide recommendations to program leadership regarding resident eligibility and approval, as appropriate.
Oversee the administration and facilitation of the annual In-Training Examination, ensuring appropriate planning, coordination, compliance with examination requirements, and successful execution.
Work with the Assistant Director of Education, Assistant Director of Finance, and Department Administrator to oversee, review, and maintain the overall Education budget and program-specific budgets. Monitor spending and budget performance, identify and communicate anticipated needs or variances, and recommend appropriate use and allocation of funds to support educational programs and priorities. Manage the GME Admin account, including but not limited to:
Coordinate submission of resident book fund and conference stipend requests. Track resident spending and available balances for these stipends.

ii. Coordinate reimbursements and requisitions for residency and education-related expenses.

iii. Monitor education-related expenditures and available funds throughout the fiscal year and provide recommendations regarding budget utilization, anticipated expenses, and opportunities to support educational initiatives.

In collaboration with the Finance Coordinator, they are responsible for tracking each housestaff members use of the transportation benefit and ensuring compliance with applicable tax policies. This includes maintaining accurate records, sending monthly communications, and taking any necessary action to ensure ongoing compliance.
Partner with program leadership to coordinate and oversee the implementation of resident remediation and performance improvement plans, ensuring appropriate documentation, tracking of requirements and milestones, timely follow-up, and adherence to institutional and GME policies.
Ensure all necessary documentation for each rotating site is up to date as well as oversee the management of out- electives (including malpractice insurance).
Collaborate with and provide operational support to members of the EM Education Team as needed, contributing to cross-program initiatives, departmental priorities, and continuity of education operations.
Partner with the Vice Chair for Education to plan the annual Grand Rounds speaker series, including identifying and recommending prospective speakers and coordinating speaker visits. Maintain and regularly update a pipeline of prospective speakers based on recommendations received throughout the year and provide recommendations for consideration during annual Grand Rounds planning.
Manage the Department of Emergency Medicine Grand Rounds program, overseeing all aspects of planning and execution. Ensure the annual calendar and speaker schedule are established and maintained; oversee speaker communications, logistics, and required financial processes; and coordinate activities leading up to and on the day of each Grand Rounds session to ensure successful execution.
Oversee the CME application and administration process for departmental educational programming, ensuring timely submission, appropriate documentation, and compliance with institutional CME requirements and standards.
Oversee the maintenance and management of resident files and records, ensuring documentation is accurate, complete, current, and maintained in accordance with institutional, GME, ACGME, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Develop initial drafts of GMEC proposals for review by program and departmental leadership, including reviewing requirements, recommending appropriate content and language, and incorporating relevant programmatic information. Conduct initial Balance of Trade analyses, identify potential concerns or discrepancies, and provide findings and recommendations to program leadership for review.
Oversee the residency programs web presence, ensuring content is accurate, current, and reflective of program priorities, recruitment efforts, and institutional standards.
Oversee and provide guidance to the Education Coordinator in the postgraduate verification process, ensuring requests are completed accurately and within established timelines and addressing escalated or complex requests as needed.
Oversee the maintenance of departmental education distribution lists, including resident classes, residency leadership, education leadership, and other relevant groups, ensuring information remains accurate and current.

Partner with education program leadership and key departmental stakeholders, including faculty and administrators, to assess program operations and workflows, identify opportunities for improvement, and recommend and coordinate implementation of process or programmatic changes.

Program Accreditation
Oversee the administrative management of the residency programs accreditation and compliance activities, ensuring adherence to applicable policies, procedures, and requirements of NYU Grossman School of Medicine, the GME Office, and the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME).
Maintain comprehensive and current knowledge of ACGME requirements, institutional GME policies, and accreditation standards. Interpret and

communicate relevant requirements to program leadership and education staff and provide ongoing guidance, training, and professional development to program coordinators to support continued compliance.

Oversee the administrative coordination of Clinical Competency Committee (CCC) processes, including establishing expectations and timelines for coordinators, monitoring completion of required activities, and ensuring timely and accurate submission of resident Milestones in WebADS.
Partner with the Residency Program Director, Associate Program Directors, and GME Office to plan and implement changes to the training program. Conduct initial review and analysis of proposed changes, identify applicable institutional and accreditation requirements, and coordinate processes such as GMEC proposals and Balance of Trade analyses
Oversee and project-manage the Annual Program Evaluation (APE), Program Evaluation Committee (PEC), and Program Improvement Plan (PIP) processes throughout the academic year. Maintain the annual PIP tracker, monitor progress toward identified goals and action items, and ensure appropriate follow-up and documentation.
Serve as the administrative project manager for the PEC process, proactively reviewing PIP progress and relevant program data throughout the year and partnering with the Program Director and Associate Program Directors to identify areas requiring PEC review, discussion, or action.
Review findings and recommendations resulting from APEs, internal reviews, accreditation activities, and site visits in collaboration with program leadership; coordinate implementation and tracking of resulting improvement initiatives and provide recommendations regarding appropriate administrative actions and follow-up.
Lead the administrative preparation for ACGME accreditation and institutional site visits in collaboration with the Program Director and GME Office. Establish timelines and deliverables, oversee preparation of required documentation by program coordinators, review materials for completeness and accuracy, and ensure program readiness.
Oversee GME, ACGME, and institutional survey processes, including proactively preparing and developing materials to support program leadership, faculty, and residents in advance of survey administration; ensuring accurate and timely completion; reviewing and analyzing survey results to identify trends, areas of concern, and opportunities for improvement; and providing recommendations to program leadership regarding appropriate follow-up actions and programmatic improvements.

Summary

As an Acquisition Project Manager you will lead complex, high-value Department of War or civilian agency IT and professional service acquisitions through the pre-award lifecycle, serving as the technical expert from project initiation to task order award.

Location of position:
This position is within the Federal Acquisition Service, Assisted Acquisition Services, OSO.

Serves as an expert Acquisition Project Manager and concurrently and independently leads at least one or multiple highly-complex, high-dollar ($250M+) acquisitions from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award providing technical advice to the client, contractors, and AAS regarding pre- award strategies and activities. Identifies, analyzes, strategizes, optimally schedules, and tracks acquisition milestones to ensure that the acquisition satisfies client’s mission needs.
Assesses, defines, and documents client technical and contractual requirements which can include state of the art or unprecedented needs. Conducts market research and identifies the optimal acquisition strategy to accomplish the client requirement. Incorporates acquisition best practices to satisfy client needs. Solves complex acquisition challenges that may arise during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle.
Translates client requirements and acquisition strategy into written documentation. Prepares the solicitation and related acquisition documents in accordance with the approved acquisition strategy. Uses expert acquisition and analytical knowledge, writes technical evaluation reports summarizing the Technical Evaluation Board findings.
Develops and maintains partnerships with clients, contractor support staff, and other GSA employees. Works with the Contracting Officer to solicit competition and provide fair opportunity through industry engagement activities such as Industry Day, Reading Rooms, and Due Diligence.
Provides leadership to matrixed Integrated Project Teams during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle. Coordinates team responsibilities, manages client expectations, resolves complex acquisition issues, mentors junior staff, and ensures acquisition documentation and project files are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

US Citizenship or National (Residents of American Samoa and Swains Island)
Meet all eligibility criteria within 30 days of the closing date
Meet time-in-grade within 30 days of the closing date, if applicable
Register with Selective Service if you are a male born after 12/31/1959
Requires temporary duty business travel approximately 25% of the time.

Undergo and pass a background investigation (Tier 2 investigation level).

Name, address, telephone number, email address;
Job Title (if Federal Service, provide series and grade; if not in GS plan, provide GS equivalent grade);
Relevant work experience—should include employer name, job title, start and end dates (month/year), the number of hours worked per week and descriptions that explain how you meet the required qualifications in the job announcement.
Education, certifications or licensures—If the job announcement requires any education, certifications or licensures, make sure to include the required information and any required documents like transcripts.

Your resume should contain enough information to make a valid determination that you fully meet experience requirements for each grade level you are applying to. If you do not provide enough information for us to determine your qualifications, you may be rated ineligible.

If you have volunteered your service through a National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, Americorps), we encourage you to apply and include this experience on your resume.

The GS-13
salary range starts at $106,437per year. If you are a new federal employee, your starting salary will likely be set at the Step 1 of the grade for which you are selected.

To qualify, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or higher in the Federal service. Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated expertise in Federal acquisition and project management, specifically from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award. Such experience must include:

Providing technical advice; identifying and developing customer agency requirements;
Preparing and documenting the acquisition strategy;
Preparing statements of work and/or performance work statements;
Determining contract type; and
Leading the technical evaluation of proposals.

Additional vacancies may be filled through this announcement in this or other GSA organizations within the same commuting area as needed; through other means; or not at all.

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.

new_jobs.title: Power Systems Project Manager, Data Center Focus
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Power Systems Project Manager, Data Center Focus

Boston, MA | Syracuse, NY | Arlington, VA | Chicago, IL | Houston, TX | Hybrid

Are you a project delivery leader who wants to help shape how the country's fastest-growing power consumers get connected to the grid? Do you want to own the schedule, budget, and client relationship on high-visibility data center and mission-critical power projects, instead of just contributing to them? Are you energized by leading multi-disciplinary teams through the full lifecycle of a project, from early-stage feasibility through construction support?

If this sounds like you, or you're curious to learn more, then this role could be the perfect opportunity. Join our Power Systems Department as our new Power Systems Project Manager, Data Center Focus, and work with us to close the gap to a sustainable future.

About Ramboll

Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a foundation-owned people company. We have more than 18,000 experts working across our global operations in 35 countries. Our experts are leaders in their fields, developing and delivering innovative solutions in diverse markets including Buildings, Transport, Planning & Urban Design, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, and Management Consulting. We invite you to contribute to a more sustainable future working in an open, collaborative, and empowering company. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we together shape the societies of tomorrow.

Job Description

Your new role

As our new Power Systems Project Manager, Data Center Focus, you will take full ownership of project planning, execution, and delivery for a growing portfolio of data center, mission-critical, and pre-investment infrastructure clients. You will manage scope, schedule, and budget across multi-disciplinary engagements spanning substation design, generation and load interconnection, and early-stage site feasibility, serving as the primary point of contact for clients who often have limited in-house experience navigating energy infrastructure development.

You will work closely with our technical leads across substation engineering, protection and control, and interconnection to keep integrated, constructible designs on track, while also representing Ramboll directly with investors, property developers, and economic development agencies evaluating pre-investment opportunities.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Own project plans, schedules, and budgets for data center and mission-critical power engagements, tracking performance against milestones and financial targets and driving corrective action when needed

Serve as the primary client contact for data center developers, investors, property developers, and economic development agencies, translating client objectives into actionable project scope and guiding clients with limited energy-infrastructure experience through the development pathway

Lead multi-disciplinary coordination across substation design, protection and control, civil/structural, power generation, and interconnection disciplines to ensure integrated, constructible project delivery

Manage subconsultants, vendors, and contract administration in support of assigned projects

Support early-stage feasibility studies, power availability assessments, and preliminary master planning for pre-investment and greenfield data center site opportunities

Identify and manage project risks, developing and tracking mitigation strategies in coordination with technical leads

Lead preparation of proposals, fee estimates, and client presentations, contributing to business development for the data center and mission-critical client segment

Ensure compliance with Ramboll QA/QC procedures and applicable industry standards throughout project execution

Mentor Assistant Project Managers and early-career staff supporting your projects

Coordinate with our Interconnection and Substation Engineering teams to ensure client-facing commitments are technically grounded and deliverable

Your new team

You will be part of an elite team of power system engineers and play a pivotal role in delivering advanced solutions for a wide variety of clients, including energy-intensive industries like semiconductor manufacturing, municipal entities, data center mega campuses, and pioneers in renewable energy. With our substantial growth, seize the opportunity to shape our strategy and contribute to our agile team's rich pipeline of projects.

With growth horizons in cutting-edge domains like HVDC, solar photovoltaics, and offshore wind, our energetic and inventive team, bolstered by global specialists, is committed to advancing Ramboll's reach across the US, notably in states championing progressive climate objectives and sustainability measures. At the heart of our mission is the conviction that electricity is the cornerstone of the green transition toward a carbon-neutral future. Join us in our unwavering pursuit to realize this vision.

Qualifications

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills, and capabilities that will set you up for success.

These include:

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Power Systems Engineering, or a closely related field

7+ years of experience in power systems or electrical infrastructure project delivery, with demonstrated ownership of project scope, schedule, and budget

Experience supporting data center, mission-critical, or large-load client engagements is strongly preferred

Working knowledge of substation design, power generation, generation/load interconnection processes, and transmission planning fundamentals

Familiarity with ISO/RTO interconnection queue processes (e.g., ISO-NE, NYISO, PJM) and their implications for project schedule and risk is a plus

Demonstrated ability to manage multi-disciplinary teams and subconsultants on complex infrastructure projects

PMP certification, or active pursuit of PMP, is a plus

Professional Engineering (PE) license is a plus but not required

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to advise clients who have limited energy-infrastructure development experience

Proven track record contributing to proposals, fee estimation, and business development

What We Can Offer You

Flexible work environment

Investment in your development

Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles

Be valued for the unique person you are

Never be short of inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects

The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Direct exposure to Ramboll's fastest-growing client segment: data centers, mission-critical power, and pre-investment infrastructure development

Additional Information

Ready to join us?

Please submit your application. Be sure to include all relevant documents including your CV, cover letter, etc.

Work at the heart of sustainable change

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. We believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. At Ramboll, our core strength is our people, and our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act. Being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. We embrace an inclusive mindset that looks for fresh, diverse, and innovative perspectives. We respect, embrace, and invite diversity in all forms to actively cultivate an environment where everyone can flourish and realize their full potential.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $120,000 to $140,000 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Thank you for taking the time to apply! We look forward to receiving your application.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Job Summary

Randstad is seeking a highly autonomous IT Program Manager - Real Estate & Facilities Technology to lead enterprise technology delivery for our client's Corporate Real Estate, Stations, Facilities & Accessibility (SFA), and Properties divisions. In this pivotal role, you will bridge the gap between enterprise IT and corporate real estate operations, driving the roadmap for integrated workplace management systems (IWMS), lease administration, capital program tracking, asset maintenance, CAD/BIM, and forward-looking workplace solutions. The ideal candidate pairs traditional waterfall program governance-including milestone baselining, phase-gate enforcement, and rigorous accrual-based financial forecasting-with the technical acumen to align business goals, manage third-party vendor project managers, and deliver scalable enterprise systems with minimal oversight.

location: Washington, Washington, D.C.

job type: Contract

salary: $75 - 85 per hour

work hours: 9am to 5pm

education: Bachelors

Responsibilities

Program Governance & Delivery:
Own the end-to-end delivery of the Real Estate Technology Services roadmap, tracking project milestones, managing phase-gate reviews, and monitoring performance variance against established schedule baselines.

Financial Management & Accruals:
Manage project financials using accrual-based accounting principles; synthesize, model, and submit comprehensive monthly forecasts covering internal labor, vendor spend, and capital expenditures.

Domain Initiatives Oversight:
Lead technology delivery across key real estate functional areas, including asset maintenance, corporate lease accounting/administration, space utilization, energy and sustainability monitoring, CAD/BIM platforms, and digital workplace tools.

Status Reporting & Risk Management:
Maintain a disciplined cadence of monthly project status updates, actively managing risks, issue tracking, dependency logs, and executive accomplishments across internal enterprise systems.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management:
Serve as the primary IT delivery liaison to business leadership, department directors, and external software vendor project managers, ensuring strict adherence to contractual deliverables and statement of work (SOW) scope.

Cross-Functional Alignment:
Lead steering committees, executive status reviews, and cross-functional working sessions across IT, Corporate Real Estate, and Finance teams.

Qualifications

Experience: Minimum 5+ years of progressive project or program management experience leading IT implementations within Corporate Real Estate (CRE), Facilities Management, or Capital Program operations.

Financial Acumen: Strong, demonstrated experience with accrual-based project accounting, budget variance reporting, and corporate monthly financial forecasting.

Certifications: PMP (Project Management Professional) certification is strongly preferred; candidates must demonstrate solid grounding in traditional waterfall milestone and schedule governance.

Software & Tool Proficiency

Capital Program & Project Management: Hands-on experience with enterprise capital program tools such as EPPM Masterworks (or comparable tools like e-Builder, Primavera P6, or Oracle Unifier).

Data & Analytics: Advanced, mastery-level proficiency in Microsoft Excel (complex financial modeling, pivot tables, forecasting, and data analysis).

Collaboration & PM Tools: Proven working proficiency with SharePoint, Microsoft Project, Jira, and Confluence.

Real Estate Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with Corporate Real Estate enterprise software (e.g., IWMS, Tririga, Archibus, Planon, or similar lease administration, building management, and space planning solutions).

Communication & Autonomy: Exceptional communication, executive presentation, and vendor coordination skills, with a proven ability to operate independently with high initiative and minimal daily direction.

Location & Availability: Must be based within the greater Washington, D.C. (or Philadelphia) metropolitan area to participate in local meetings and key team planning sessions as required.

Help

You will oversee all phases of the Spectrum Management process.
You will guarantee that the DON Spectrum Planning Subsystem (SPS) Certification and Frequency Assignment processes adhere to the established timeframes of the DoD and National Telecommunication and Information Administration (NTIA).
You will ensure the maximum feasible compatibility of all electromagnetic devices, equipment, and systems within the DON and with other government and non-government users of the electromagnetic spectrum.
You will provide comprehensive supervisory guidance and direction to the NMSC Deputy Director, Division Heads, team managers, and support personnel.

Requirements

Help

Conditions of employment

Must be a US Citizen.
Must be determined suitable for federal employment.
Must participate in the direct deposit pay program.
New employees to the Department of the Navy will be required to successfully pass the E-Verify employment verification check. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, visit e-verify.gov
Generally, current federal employees applying for GS jobs must serve at least one year at the next lower grade level. This requirement is called time-in-grade. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement.
Within the Department of Defense (DoD), the appointment of retired military members within 180 days immediately following retirement date to a civilian position is subject to the provisions of 5 United States Code 3326.
Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered for Selective Service.
You will be required to obtain and maintain an interim and/or final security clearance prior to entrance on duty. Failure to obtain and maintain the required level of clearance may result in the withdrawal of a job offer or removal.
MSP/PPP applicants must currently hold the required security clearance.
Successful completion of a pre-employment drug test (including marijuana) is required. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if you fail to report to the drug test appointment or fail the test. You will be subject to random testing.
This position may require travel from normal duty station to CONUS and OCONUS and may include remote or isolated sites. You must be able to travel on military and commercial aircraft for extended periods of time.
You will be required to obtain and maintain a U.S. Passport.
This position is considered Key/Emergency-Essential. You will be required to provide immediate and continuing support to ensure the success of combat operations or the availability of combat-essential systems.
This is a Mission Essential position. You will be required to ensure organization or facility continuity of operations and/or completion of tasks that are considered essential to the mission designated by a local or command decision.
You may be required to report to work or remain at work to perform essential functions during contingency operations, natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, or other emergency situations.
Frequent driving is necessary to attend national-level meetings and conferences, necessitating a substantial quantity of local travel. International engagements necessitate an average of six annual travels abroad.
The sensitivity, importance, and fast-paced nature of the responsibilities generate significant stress and strain.

Qualifications

Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-14 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following:

Experience with extensive background in the supervision and administration of communications-electronics systems.
Experience in electromagnetic spectrum and operations and spectrum management.
Experience demonstrating comprehensive knowledge of radio frequency spectrum management principles, national and international frequency coordination, equipment spectrum certification, electromagnetic compatibility, host-nation coordination, interference resolution, and spectrum support to military operations.
Experience in interacting with frequency management authorities across a variety of Department of Defense (DoD) agencies and departments.

new_jobs.description:
Summary

As an Acquisition Project Manager you will lead complex, high-value Department of War or civilian agency IT and professional service acquisitions through the pre-award lifecycle, serving as the technical expert from project initiation to task order award.

Location of position:
This position is within the Federal Acquisition Service, Assisted Acquisition Services, OSO.

We are currently filling four vacancies, but additional vacancies may be filled as needed.

Learn more about this agency

Duties

Serves as an expert Acquisition Project Manager and concurrently and independently leads at least one or multiple highly-complex, high-dollar ($250M+) acquisitions from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award providing technical advice to the client, contractors, and AAS regarding pre- award strategies and activities. Identifies, analyzes, strategizes, optimally schedules, and tracks acquisition milestones to ensure that the acquisition satisfies client’s mission needs.
Assesses, defines, and documents client technical and contractual requirements which can include state of the art or unprecedented needs. Conducts market research and identifies the optimal acquisition strategy to accomplish the client requirement. Incorporates acquisition best practices to satisfy client needs. Solves complex acquisition challenges that may arise during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle.
Translates client requirements and acquisition strategy into written documentation. Prepares the solicitation and related acquisition documents in accordance with the approved acquisition strategy. Uses expert acquisition and analytical knowledge, writes technical evaluation reports summarizing the Technical Evaluation Board findings.
Develops and maintains partnerships with clients, contractor support staff, and other GSA employees. Works with the Contracting Officer to solicit competition and provide fair opportunity through industry engagement activities such as Industry Day, Reading Rooms, and Due Diligence.
Provides leadership to matrixed Integrated Project Teams during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle. Coordinates team responsibilities, manages client expectations, resolves complex acquisition issues, mentors junior staff, and ensures acquisition documentation and project files are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.

Requirements

US Citizenship or National (Residents of American Samoa and Swains Island)
Meet all eligibility criteria within 30 days of the closing date
Meet time-in-grade within 30 days of the closing date, if applicable

Job Title (if Federal Service, provide series and grade; if not in GS plan, provide GS equivalent grade);
Relevant work experience—should include employer name, job title, start and end dates (month/year), the number of hours worked per week and descriptions that explain how you meet the required qualifications in the job announcement.

If you have volunteered your service through a National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, Americorps), we encourage you to apply and include this experience on your resume.

The GS-13
salary range starts at $106,437per year. If you are a new federal employee, your starting salary will likely be set at the Step 1 of the grade for which you are selected.

To qualify, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or higher in the Federal service. Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated expertise in Federal acquisition and project management, specifically from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award. Such experience must include:

Providing technical advice; identifying and developing customer agency requirements;
Preparing and documenting the acquisition strategy;
Preparing statements of work and/or performance work statements;
Determining contract type; and
Leading the technical evaluation of proposals.

Applicants are encouraged to make their resume searchable in their USAJOBS.gov profile. This will allow Federal hiring specialists and hiring managers across agencies to find their resume as part of agency recruitment campaigns or staffing searches.

If you apply to this position and are selected, we will not ask about your criminal history before you receive a conditional job offer. If you believe you were asked about your criminal history improperly, contact the agency or visit GSA's webpage.

Job Type:
Open & Promotional (Dual)

Definition

Plans, coordinates, budgets, and manages assigned college construction and renovation projects from the initial planning phase through final completion to ensure that projects and successfully delivered within budget, schedule, and in compliance with regulatory guidelines and District specifications.

Typical Duties

Assists college administrators with the development of building, construction, and renovation plans by meeting and consulting with architects, engineers, and appropriate college and District staff.

Provides details, technical project descriptions, and specifications for contract architects and/or architectural and engineering staff.

Gathers data, develops project budgets, and implements appropriate budgetary control procedures for all phases including design, construction, and group II equipment.

Prepares applications for projects and submits project information for review or approval to the Board of Trustees, California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office, and others.

Coordinates projects with ongoing or proposed major maintenance programs, equipment needs, land acquisition, project design, contract solicitation, project inspection, and the Division of the State Architect.

Maintains liaison with college administration throughout planning and construction phases to provide information on project operations and progress and to receive input on the plans, schedules, interests, and concerns of the college regarding the project.

Identifies and updates project risks periodically, and creates and updates risk mitigation plans.

Meets with college maintenance and operations staff to confer on matters that may impact their ability to effectively maintain and operate the facility under construction.

Responds to concerns, requests, and questions from college administration regarding the project.

Monitors the entry of data related to approved projects and facilities inventory into the District's computerized reporting system.

Provides ongoing management of multiple assigned construction/renovation projects representing the interests of college and District administrations including directions to the architect, engineer, and construction inspector, project design, implementation of budget controls, project bid ability, construct ability, bid specifications, change orders, administration of various contracts, management of the inspection, and other project management requirements during the preliminary planning, documentation bidding, and construction phases of various projects.

Assists in the review and approval of contractors' proposed construction schedules.

Assists in the review and evaluation of construction project progress and approval of requests for payment.

Monitors construction document status, submittals, and as-build drawing preparation.

Reviews requests for clarification and assists in interpretation of construction documents.

Assists in processing and negotiating cost, scheduling change orders, and resolving complex construction related disputes.

Coordinates project close-out and move-in activities.

Interfaces and assists fiscal services in reconciliation of the Capital Outlay Fund to the general ledger and the filing of claims for reimbursement.

Assists in the coordination of construction planning events with purchasing and contracts for scheduling and acquisition of equipment.

Advises commissioned architects, engineers, consultants, and contractors about District design and construction policies, requirements, and standards.

Performs related duties as assigned.

Distinguishing Characteristics

A Facilities Project Manager
plans, coordinates, budgets, and manages multiple assigned college building construction and renovation, modernization, and repair projects throughout project development, design, and construction to ensure that projects are successfully delivered within budget, schedule, and in compliance with regulatory guidelines and District specifications. The projects range in complexity and typical values of $0.2 million to $5 million.

A Construction Inspector
serves as the resident inspector for the District at construction sites; performs continuous inspection of all phases of assigned construction including materials, methods, and workmanship; and checks for compliance with plans, specifications, and regulations. An incumbent in this classification must possess a Class 1 inspector certification issued by the Division of the State Architect.

A Director of Facilities Planning and Development
assists the Chief Facilities Executive by assuming administrative and technical responsibility and authority for delegated program areas and projects; supervising daily division activities and personnel; and assuming responsibility for the Chief Facilities Executive in their absence.

Supervision

General supervision is received from the Director of Facilities Planning and Development. Functional supervision is exercised over commissioned architects, engineers, consultants, and contractors employed by the District on an assigned project.

Class Qualifications

Knowledge of:

Principles of facilities planning as related to methods and techniques of instruction, traffic flow, economy of maintenance, provision for growth, relationship of instructional and service provision of temporary facilities, and adaptability to multi-functional usage

General characteristics and relative costs of various methods of construction, architectural features, and building and room design for all types of school uses

Principles of budgetary planning and management

Characteristics and use of various methods of graphic presentation and construction documentation cartography

Construction delivery methods such as Design-Build, Design-Bid-Build, etc.

Applicable state and local building codes/regulations and review procedures

Recordkeeping procedures

Project review/approval processes

Close out requirements and processes

Capabilities of computer applications, systems, and hardware used in facilities planning and development

Ability To

Effectively structure, integrate, and control all aspects of a project including initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling, and closing

Manage a team of professionals in construction, engineering, and architectural disciplines

Maintain focus and quality under distracting working conditions and high workloads

Manage project budget and expenses in a manner consistent with achieving project quality, schedules, and levels of service

Understand audit and oversight functions and the impact of quality assurance reviews and inspection

Represent the interests of college and District administrations relative to assigned projects

Analyze and interpret complex information and make appropriate recommendations

Interpret technical materials such as building and attendance codes, standards, and regulations

Assure compliance with project requirements and standards

Anticipate conditions, plan ahead, establish priorities, and meet schedules

Act independently and promptly to situations and events

Travel to on-site and off-site meetings

Travel to various locations to monitor project progress

Prepare clear, concise, and effective oral and written communications, reports, and presentations

Maintain accurate and complete records

Effectively collaborate with external regulatory, governmental, and business or customer groups

Communicate effectively with architects, consultants, contractors, and District administrators

Effectively utilize computer equipment, software, and hardware in the performance of duties

Learn specialized software applications

A bachelor's degree from a recognized college or university, preferably with a major in architecture, construction management, engineering, urban planning, or a related field AND four years of full-time, paid, professional-level experience in planning facilities or managing the construction of educational, governmental, or commercial building projects. Experience with the project life cycle and planning and construction of educational facilities is highly desirable.

OR

Experience with the project life cycle and planning and construction of educational facilities is highly desirable.

Special

A $50,000 life insurance policy is provided free of charge for each employee.

19 paid holidays per year.

Duties

This position is with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), within U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Office of Facilities and Asset Management (OFAM),Mission Support Facilities (MSF) Division. Mission Support Facilities Division provides the facilities and associated infrastructure, facilities management, and sustainment to support CBP mission support office operations. As stewards of a large national portfolio of GSA-owned and CBP-owned infrastructure, MSF carefully balances resources to ensure the right facilities are planned and delivered at the right time to meet mission requirements. The Enterprise Facilities Support (EFS)Program Management Office (PMO) is comprised of three branches - Facilities and Infrastructure Management, Housing, and Program Management. These branches are responsible for the planning, development, and execution of facility projects, handling maintenance and repairs, and coordinating/evaluating Facility Condition Assessments for all mission support facilities outside of the National Capital Region, including CBP's portfolio of residential housing. This position starts at a salary of $106,437.00 (GS-13, Step 1) to $138,370.00 (GS-13, Step 10). Salary: Salary listed reflects the rest of U.S. scale and, if applicable, will be adjusted to meet the locality pay or cost of living expenses of the duty location upon selection. GS Salary: Visit this link to view the locality pay tables by geographic area. If you do not see your geographic area listed, select the "Rest of United States" pay table. Some positions fall under a special pay rate depending on the series, grade level and location of the position. Please visit this link to view special pay rate charts. Typical work assignments include: Coordinating collaboratively with CBP organizations that EFS services to evaluate and refine their facility requirements into formal Requirements Development Requests (RDRs). Leading the optimal conversion of RDRs into viable projects that are frequently executed by other government agencies, primarily the General Services Administration. Projects may include space expansions, contractions, reconfigurations, relocations, or upgrades to various aspects of their existing space including outdated, dilapidated or insufficient elements such as furniture, security features, or audio/visual equipment. Leading coordination with OFAM subject matter experts and applicable facility owners toward resolution of any lease related issues that arise for any leased space or maintenance and repair issues not promptly addressed. Performing occupancy cost analysis, analyzing and justifying operating expenses, maintaining accurate documentation, and resolving issues efficiently. Utilizing the automated real property program TRIRIGA to take corrective actions for users, resolve data reporting errors, and identify complex existing or potential program issues to PMO leadership, while making recommendations for timely and executable plans for corrective actions.

Requiremennts

You must be a U.S. Citizen to apply for this position Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered with Selective Service Primary U.S. residency for at least three of the last five years (additional details below) All pre-employment processes will be conducted in English You may be required to pass a background investigation CBP follows the DHS Drug-Free Workplace Plan for drug testing procedures As an employee of CBP, you will be joining a workforce that is dedicated to accomplishing our mission while maintaining the trust of our Nation by strictly adhering to all government ethics standards. Your conduct will be subject to the ethics rules applicable to all Executive Branch employees, and to CBP employees specifically, as well as the criminal conflict of interest statutes. Once you enter on duty, these rules include obtaining approval for outside employment or business activity, to ensure such employment or business activity is not prohibited and does not interfere or conflict with performance of your official duties. 213.3102(u), and/or Disabled Veterans with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more as defined by 5 CFR
315.707. Veterans, Peace Corps/VISTA volunteers, and persons with disabilities possess a wealth of unique talents, experiences, and competencies that can be invaluable to the DHS mission. If you are a member of one of these groups, you may not have to compete with the public for federal jobs. To determine your eligibility for non-competitive appointment and to understand the required documentation, click on the links above or contact the Servicing Human Resources Office listed at the bottom of this announcement.

Qualifications

Experience: You qualify for the GS-13 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Implementing and monitoring maintenance, repair, and operations programs. Performing analytical studies related to programming, budget planning, financial management, project control, acquisition of supplies and equipment logistics management, security management, staff management, and information technology support. Advising management and other stakeholders on the results and implications of strategic planning studies and analyses and making recommendations for process improvement. Measuring program and project performance, developing data-driven recommendations for improvement, and implementing new program strategies and methodologies to enhance efficiency and effectiveness. NOTE: Your resume must explicitly indicate how you meet this requirement, otherwise you will be found ineligible. Please see the "Required Documents" section below for additional resume requirements. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Background Investigation: U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is a federal law enforcement agency that requires all applicants to undergo a thorough background investigation prior to employment in order to promote the agency's core values of vigilance, service to country, and integrity. During the screening and/or background investigation process, you will be asked questions regarding any felony criminal convictions or current felony charges, the use of illegal drugs (e.g., marijuana, cocaine, heroin, LSD, methamphetamines, ecstasy), and the use of non-prescribed controlled substances including any experimentation, possession, sale, receipt, manufacture, cultivation, production, transfer, shipping, trafficking, or distribution of controlled substances. new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Data Transformation
new_jobs.description:
Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

As Program Manager, Data Transformation, you will run the day-to-day program engine that turns Oura's business data into governed, trusted, decision-ready metrics. You will work inside the Data Transformation program, alongside the Staff Program Manager, and own the delivery rhythm for your assigned data domains: intake, prioritization, tracking, ownership, certification, and reporting. Early focus areas include Hardware and Supply Chain, where the need for structure is greatest.A core part of the job is metric certification and intake discipline. You will enforce the three-path model for every request and metric: Directional (fit for use, fast), Governed (executive, board, investor, or external numbers, with a certification path), and Not ours (operational or application work rerouted to the owning business team). You will also drive the work itself, including sprints where they help, so certification and delivery commitments actually land.Hardware and supply chain data, for example, spans manufacturing, quality, logistics, sourcing, planning, and new product introduction. This role connects those teams to Data Engineering and Analytics so that the numbers executives, finance, and auditors rely on (for example warranty rate, click-to-delivery, and yield) have one definition, one owner, and a clear path from directional to governed to certified.This role is ideal for a program manager who is comfortable in ambiguity, can read a data pipeline diagram as easily as a project plan, and likes bringing structure to fast-moving, cross-functional work.

What You Will Do

Take business metrics from informally tracked to fully certified, each with a locked definition, a single accountable owner, and documented lineage and controls
Make sure every key metric in your domains has a clear owner and approver, and keep that ownership current as the business changes
Triage incoming data requests by their intended use and level of rigor, and route work that belongs to other teams to the right place
Run a structured intake process with clear priorities, business justification, and reliable response times
Drive cross-functional programs to completion across Data Engineering, Finance, Supply Chain, Hardware, and IT, using agile practices where they help
Keep program plans accurate and visible, with named leads, dates, and status that stakeholders can trust
Track data issues and metric regressions through to resolution, and support documentation for internal and external audit
Communicate progress and data health clearly to senior leaders, and drive adoption of standardized metric definitions

This is a hybrid role out of our San Francisco office.

What You'll Bring

5 to 8 years of experience in program management, technical program management, or business operations, including time supporting data, analytics, or operations teams
Experience running cross-functional programs with many stakeholders and competing priorities, without formal authority
Experience with metric governance or controls work: definitions, ownership, documentation, and formal sign-off
Comfortable working in Databricks or a similar lakehouse: can navigate the catalog, read a SQL query or model to understand how a metric is computed, and spot-check numbers against source tables
Working understanding of data pipelines and transformation layers (dbt or equivalent): can follow lineage from source system to reported number and explain where a metric is computed
Experience with data quality controls: defining validation tests, reading test results, and tracing failures to root cause
Comfort holding a process line with senior stakeholders, including redirecting requests, while keeping relationships intact
Hands-on experience with work tracking tools such as Jira, and with running sprints or lightweight agile cadences
Clear written and verbal communication, including status reporting for senior audiences

Nice To Have

Experience with hardware, manufacturing, quality, logistics, sourcing, or supply planning
Background in consumer hardware, wearables, medical devices, or another regulated hardware business
Exposure to financial reporting, SOX-style controls, audit preparation, or IPO readiness
Experience at a high-growth or pre-IPO company
Experience working with distributed teams across US and European time zones
Comfort using modern AI tooling to speed up analysis, documentation, and reporting

Benefits

At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health.

What We Offer

Competitive salary
Lunch benefit
Wellness benefit
Flexible working hours
Collaborative, smart teammates
An Ōura ring of your own
Wellness Time Off

new_jobs.title: Acquisition Project Manager - Federal Acquisition Service
new_jobs.description:
Summary

As an Acquisition Project Manager you will lead complex, high-value Department of War or civilian agency IT and professional service acquisitions through the pre-award lifecycle, serving as the technical expert from project initiation to task order award.

Location of position:
This position is within the Federal Acquisition Service, Assisted Acquisition Services, OSO.

We are currently filling four vacancies, but additional vacancies may be filled as needed.

Learn more about this agency

Duties

Serves as an expert Acquisition Project Manager and concurrently and independently leads at least one or multiple highly-complex, high-dollar ($250M+) acquisitions from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award providing technical advice to the client, contractors, and AAS regarding pre- award strategies and activities. Identifies, analyzes, strategizes, optimally schedules, and tracks acquisition milestones to ensure that the acquisition satisfies client’s mission needs.
Assesses, defines, and documents client technical and contractual requirements which can include state of the art or unprecedented needs. Conducts market research and identifies the optimal acquisition strategy to accomplish the client requirement. Incorporates acquisition best practices to satisfy client needs. Solves complex acquisition challenges that may arise during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle.
Translates client requirements and acquisition strategy into written documentation. Prepares the solicitation and related acquisition documents in accordance with the approved acquisition strategy. Uses expert acquisition and analytical knowledge, writes technical evaluation reports summarizing the Technical Evaluation Board findings.
Develops and maintains partnerships with clients, contractor support staff, and other GSA employees. Works with the Contracting Officer to solicit competition and provide fair opportunity through industry engagement activities such as Industry Day, Reading Rooms, and Due Diligence.
Provides leadership to matrixed Integrated Project Teams during the pre-award acquisition lifecycle. Coordinates team responsibilities, manages client expectations, resolves complex acquisition issues, mentors junior staff, and ensures acquisition documentation and project files are complete, accurate, and maintained in accordance with applicable policies and procedures.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

US Citizenship or National (Residents of American Samoa and Swains Island)
Meet all eligibility criteria within 30 days of the closing date
Meet time-in-grade within 30 days of the closing date, if applicable
Register with Selective Service if you are a male born after 12/31/1959
Requires temporary duty business travel approximately 25% of the time.

If selected, you must meet the following conditions:

Current or Former Political Appointees: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C or Non­Career SES employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the HR Office. Failure to disclose this information could result in disciplinary action including removal from Federal Service.
Serve a one year probationary period, if required.
Undergo and pass a background investigation (Tier 2 investigation level).
Have your identity and work status eligibility verified if you are not a GSA employee. We will use the Department of Homeland Security’s e-Verify system for this. Any discrepancies must be resolved as a condition of continued employment.
Complete a financial disclosure report to verify that no conflict, or an appearance of conflict, exists between your financial interest and this position.

Qualifications

To evaluate your qualifications, your resume must clearly demonstrate how you meet the specialized experience described below.
Your resume must not exceed two pages. To ensure your qualifications can be fully evaluated, we recommend including the following information:

Name, address, telephone number, email address;
Job Title (if Federal Service, provide series and grade; if not in GS plan, provide GS equivalent grade);
Relevant work experience—should include employer name, job title, start and end dates (month/year), the number of hours worked per week and descriptions that explain how you meet the required qualifications in the job announcement.
Education, certifications or licensures—If the job announcement requires any education, certifications or licensures, make sure to include the required information and any required documents like transcripts.

Your resume should contain enough information to make a valid determination that you fully meet experience requirements for each grade level you are applying to. If you do not provide enough information for us to determine your qualifications, you may be rated ineligible.

If you have volunteered your service through a National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, Americorps), we encourage you to apply and include this experience on your resume.

The GS-13
salary range starts at $106,437per year. If you are a new federal employee, your starting salary will likely be set at the Step 1 of the grade for which you are selected.

To qualify, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or higher in the Federal service. Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated expertise in Federal acquisition and project management, specifically from acquisition initiation through contract or Task Order award. Such experience must include:

Providing technical advice; identifying and developing customer agency requirements;
Preparing and documenting the acquisition strategy;
Preparing statements of work and/or performance work statements;
Determining contract type; and
Leading the technical evaluation of proposals.

Additional information

Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin.

Applicants are encouraged to make their resume searchable in their USAJOBS.gov profile. This will allow Federal hiring specialists and hiring managers across agencies to find their resume as part of agency recruitment campaigns or staffing searches.

If you apply to this position and are selected, we will not ask about your criminal history before you receive a conditional job offer. If you believe you were asked about your criminal history improperly, contact the agency or visit GSA's webpage.

Additional vacancies may be filled through this announcement in this or other GSA organizations within the same commuting area as needed; through other means; or not at all.

Relocation-related expenses are not approved and will be your responsibility.

Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.

Benefits

A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. Opens in a new windowLearn more about federal benefits.

You will have access to many benefits including:

Health insurance (choose from a wide range of plans)
Life insurance coverage with several options
Sick leave and vacation time, including 11 paid holidays per year
Thrift Savings Plan (similar to a 401(k) plan)
Transit and child care subsidies
Flexible spending accounts
Long-term care insurance
Training and development

Eligibility for benefits depends on the type of position you hold and whether your position is full-time, part-time or intermittent. Contact the hiring agency for more information on the specific benefits offered.
